name: Build Placement
description: Grid-snapped placement of shelters, furniture, and workbenches as a player verb: ghost preview, validity rules (support, clearance, slope), and material consumption on confirm. It is the survival cousin of presentation.object_placer — object_placer is a level-authoring tool that answers to a designer, while this answers to a player carrying limited wood, so it owns costs, rejection, and refunds that the authoring tool never needs. Materials leave through inventory.core_inventory BEFORE the ghost turns solid, so a placement can never duplicate resources, and removal refunds a fixed fraction through the same door. Structural logic — does this wall hold that roof — is a rules callback the game supplies; this component owns the transaction, not architecture.

inputs.name: gridSize
inputs.description: Snap increment in world units, matched to world.tile_grid's cell size. Free placement (0) is supported but off by default — the grid is what makes player-built bases readable instead of soup.

inputs.name: maxSlopeDegrees
inputs.description: Steepest terrain the ghost stays valid on. Beyond it placement is rejected rather than compensated, because auto-leveling terrain under a player's build is a silent world edit.

inputs.name: requireSupport
inputs.description: Whether elevated pieces must trace to ground through other placed pieces. The floating-castle exploit is charming exactly once; after that it is a bug report.

inputs.name: snapRotationDegrees
inputs.description: Rotation increment per rotate input. 45 degrees gives diagonals without inviting the micro-angle fiddling that a free rotate would.

inputs.name: refundFractionOnRemove
inputs.description: Fraction of materials returned when the player removes their own structure. Below 1 by design: full refunds make bases infinitely rearrangeable and delete the commitment that makes building a survival decision.

outputs.name: ghostValid
outputs.description: Whether the current ghost would place if confirmed this tick. UI renders red or green from this; the confirm path re-validates independently, so this is presentation, not authority.

outputs.name: placedCount
outputs.description: Structures placed by this placer instance. Telemetry and build-limit caps read it; the count itself enforces nothing.
